card.name: Words that open a two-sided choice
card.fires_on: The word "either" (also "what", "whether they") right where a sentence is about to set out two opposite options or outcomes, such as increase or decrease, with or without food.

modes.label: either before alternatives
modes.description: "either" introduces a pair of options such as with or without food, or increase or decrease.
modes.example: Drugs that may<< either>> increase or decrease phenytoin serum

modes.label: what was done right
modes.description: A word that starts a review of what went right versus wrong.
modes.example: Seeing<< what>> was done right, what could have been

modes.label: whether clause
modes.description: A word inside a "whether... or not" clause that sets up two cases.
modes.example: which, whether<< they>> are Catholics or not, affects their fortunes

card.writes: It nudges the model toward positive-side words like strengths, successes and positive, and away from negative.
card.plain: It fires at words that set up a pair of opposites, like "either with or without food", and leans toward the positive side.
